# Native field systems: roaming encounters, travel and supplies

The October 25 expansion keeps all eight story missions and adds six optional native map areas. The room authoring file now supplies 20 mission rooms and 23 visible encounter groups. Enemies follow short, map-checked native tile routes. Press A near one, or touch one, to start its actual native combat. Each visible enemy has a separate battle slot; this fixes the earlier shared-slot bug in which multiple field sprites could share one HP/AI record.

Returning to the Kiln renews ordinary patrol encounters. Returning also includes resting and regrouping after a mission. Moving between dungeon rooms does not renew them, and the reload immediately after winning a patrol does not renew them. Objectives, dialogue prerequisites, caches, bosses, recruits and ending state remain persistent. A defeat heals and returns the crew to that room's entrance without marking the encounter won. This is bounded visible patrol behavior, not proximity-based hunting AI.

The Kiln outfitter stands at tile (58,24), beside the arrival area. Its native dialogue menus offer six Tonics for 75 credits, an Ether and Revive for 90, an early weapon pack for 300 and three BronzeMail for 180. From mission five, the equipment choices become the veteran weapon pack for 600 and three Titan Vests for 450. Items enter the real native inventory; equip them through the native equipment menu. Resting remains free through the original hub menu. Purchases do not alter the story's existing automatic equipment rewards.

The field-route guide stands at (52,24). The first native menu selects lower city, upper city, engine frontier or return. Each submenu offers the appropriate regions. Only regions whose mission number is at most the current story phase can be entered. Visiting an earlier region does not change phase. Its defeated story boss stays hidden and its contact/director functions cannot replay the reward or debrief. The original completed-game memory-echo encounter remains available in Furnace Nine.

Progress uses the existing mission bytes 7F:01E1–01E8 and explicit expansion bytes 7F:01F0–01F7. The expansion byte for each mission uses bit 0 for its optional patrol, bit 1 for the optional one-time equipment cache and bit 2 for optional-room arrival text. Renewal masks are generated from `repeatable: true` patrols only. The compiler rejects overlap between a renewable bit and an entry, objective, NPC prerequisite, cache or permanent encounter. It also rejects unreserved flag bytes, out-of-range patrol settings and enemy battle-slot collisions. New Game clears these reserved bytes; Continue retains them.

A patrol authoring object retains `type`, `bit`, `enemies`, `stats` and optional native rewards. Set `repeatable: true` for renewal, `flag_address` for its expansion byte, and `roam` to two through eight [dx,dy] offsets relative to each member's authored tile. Speed defaults to 16 and pause to 0.35 seconds. The room authoring audit checks each route against walkable map tiles; the compiler also validates coordinates and emits yielding native movement commands rather than page-side simulation or WRAM writes. Caches can use the same explicit `flag_address` contract. Rooms can choose `entry_flag_address` for their entry-text bit.

Compile with the original private ROM and pinned tools as before. The sparse recipe and ROM hash must be regenerated together. Python checks in `test_encounters.py` verify safe state allocation, renewal protection, native movement back-edge instruction boundaries and unique per-object enemy battle slots. Controller-only gameplay checks are separate evidence; static compilation alone does not prove every path playable or establish a measured performance result.
